tasks.short: File and check personnel documents in AFAS: contracts, certificates, leave forms, evaluations, grievances.

today.trigger: A document arrives by mail, Teams or paper from a manager, employee, recruiter or agency.
steps: Open the attachment and work out which employee and document type it is
Check it is complete and signed and the dates match AFAS
Rename it and upload it to the AFAS dossier under the right category
Update the related fields in AFAS, such as the end date of a leave or a certificate expiry
Chase the sender if anything is missing
today.time_sinks: Incomplete or unsigned documents that bounce back and forth, and scans from the shop floor that are hard to read.

lenses.faster: Classification, renaming, filing and field extraction disappear; the administrator checks a pre-filled card per document in about a minute instead of five to ten.
lenses.autonomous: A document landing in the HR mailbox or AFAS starts it; a model reads type, employee and dates, rules validate them against AFAS, clean ones are filed and the rest go to an exceptions queue.
lenses.ambitious: Dossier completeness checked every night for all employees and the 150-300 flex workers, so a missing VCA or forklift certificate shows up before a shift, not at an audit; demand would grow as site managers start relying on it.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses renaming scans and typing dates; the administrator wants more time to sort out the odd cases, such as a grievance that needs care.
lenses.options: Little value in several drafts; filing is right or wrong.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from filing to running the exceptions queue and owning the document categories and validation rules, with the right to reject or return incomplete documents; slightly more expert.
reach: Learning and Development Specialist: tracking certificate expiry from Studytube against roster needs (learn the certification rules per role)
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: maintaining AFAS dossier categories and data-quality checks (learn AFAS configuration)

tasks.human_edge: Grievances, performance evaluations and leave documents that touch health or conflict need judgement on what goes in the file, who may see it, and when to involve the HR Business Partner.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call turns a messy document into checkable fields; deterministic rules then validate against AFAS inside a fixed filing flow.

in_practice.trigger: New attachment in the HR mailbox, AFAS upload or Teams channel.
steps: Model classifies document type and matches the employee by name, number and date of birth
Model extracts dates, signatures present and key fields
Rules compare the fields with AFAS and check completeness
Clean documents are filed with the standard name; exceptions go to the queue with the reason
Administrator approves or returns exceptions to the sender with a pre-written request
in_practice.human_gate: Administrator approves every exception and every grievance, evaluation or leave document before it counts; routine certificates file automatically once accuracy is proven.
systems: AFAS Profit (Jonas or an external model call)
data_needed: Document category list with required fields
Sample of labelled historic documents for testing
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS dossier audit trail plus an exceptions log in SharePoint

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 Jonas reads documents into dossier fields
Document-to-fields extraction with validation is a routine model task

risks: Wrong employee match puts a document in someone else's file (AVG breach)
Health details in leave documents entering a model prompt (GDPR Art. 9)
No published error rate for Jonas
research_questions: What share of last quarter's documents would Jonas classify and extract correctly on a sample of 200?
Can health-related leave documents be routed around the model entirely?
Does the works council see this as processing personal data needing consent under WOR art. 27(1)(k)?

tasks.short: Type employee data into AFAS: address changes, hours, absences, terminations and reasons, manager reports.

today.trigger: An employee, manager, agency or payroll sends a change by mail, form or Excel.
steps: Read the change request and find the employee in AFAS
Type the change into the right AFAS field or workflow
Check effective dates against the payroll month close
Confirm to the requester
Fix errors flagged later by payroll
drudgery: Correcting typos payroll finds at month close
today.time_sinks: Corrections after payroll runs and requests that arrive outside AFAS self-service.

lenses.faster: Typing disappears where employees and managers use AFAS Pocket and self-service, and mailed changes are pre-filled by a model; review per change drops to under a minute.
lenses.autonomous: A self-service change or a mail starts it; validated changes post to AFAS automatically, and anything touching pay, termination or dates in a closed payroll period waits for approval.
lenses.ambitious: Flex worker hours and absences from the three agency portals reconciled with AFAS every week instead of at invoice time, serving site managers who now see flex data late; demand would grow if it were cheap.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses re-keying addresses; the administrator wants more time to fix root causes of recurring payroll corrections.
lenses.options: Not useful; one correct record is the goal.
lenses.altitude: The week becomes checking a short exceptions list and owning field-level validation rules with the Payroll Specialist; the job moves to data steward, somewhat more expert.
reach: Payroll Specialist: pre-close checks of mutations before the pay run (learn the payroll cut-off and CAO pay elements)
Bookkeeper: matching agency hours to agency invoices (learn the agency rate cards)

tasks.human_edge: Termination reasons and dates carry legal and CAO consequences (notice periods, transition payment), so the person checks them and asks the manager when the story does not add up.
tasks.pattern_why: Most changes arrive in fixed forms with fixed rules; self-service plus validation rules does the work, with a model call only for free-text mails.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS self-service submission, agency portal export or mail to the HR mailbox.
steps: Self-service and portal data flow into AFAS workflows
For mails, a model call extracts the change into a structured form
Rules check format, effective date and payroll period
Clean changes post; exceptions go to the administrator
in_practice.human_gate: Administrator approves terminations, pay-related changes and anything back-dated into a closed period; the rest posts with spot checks.

evidence.claim: New hires and employees submit data in the AFAS Pocket app
Self-service and validated workflows remove most re-keying of personnel changes

risks: Warehouse staff without easy app access keep using paper
Back-dated changes slipping into a closed payroll month
Agency export formats changing without notice
research_questions: What share of current changes arrive by mail versus AFAS self-service, per site and shift?
How many payroll corrections per month trace back to manual entry?
Can the three agency portals export hours in a stable machine-readable format?

tasks.short: Run hires, leavers, transfers, promotions and leave as AFAS workflows and keep the records right.

today.trigger: A manager or HR Business Partner asks for a personnel action.
steps: Collect the details from the manager by mail or form
Start the AFAS workflow and fill contract, function, salary scale and cost centre
Generate the letter from the SharePoint template
Get signatures and file the result
Notify payroll, IT and the site
drudgery: Filling the same data into letter templates
Sending the same notices to payroll and IT
today.time_sinks: Waiting for missing information and approvals; days per action is driven by chasing, not typing.

lenses.faster: A structured request form, generated letters and automatic notices remove most typing and chasing; the administrator checks the CAO scale and dates, a few minutes per action.
lenses.autonomous: A manager request in AFAS starts it; the workflow fills fields, drafts the letter, routes approvals and nudges stalled approvers, and the administrator approves before it goes to the employee.
lenses.ambitious: Promotions and transfers for warehouse shift leads processed within one day instead of a week, a decision cycle the sites now avoid; demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses chasing managers for a cost centre; the administrator wants more time to advise managers on the right contract choice.
lenses.options: Some: for a transfer, showing two or three CAO scale placements with cost lets the manager and HRBP choose consciously.
lenses.altitude: The administrator owns the action catalogue and its templates and decides when a request is complete enough to run; more expert in CAO and contract rules.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: placing employees in the right CAO scale and step (learn both CAO pay tables)
HR Business Partner: first-line advice to managers on contract type and notice (learn the Dutch contract chain rules)

tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a 'transfer' is really a demotion, a reintegration step or a dispute, and pulling in the HRBP before it is processed.
tasks.pattern_why: Each action type has known fields, approvals and templates; rules and AFAS workflows can be written down.

in_practice.trigger: Manager submits a personnel action form in AFAS.
steps: Form enforces required fields per action type
Rules check CAO scale, contract chain and effective date
Letter generated from the SharePoint template
Approvals routed with automatic reminders
Payroll, IT and site notified on approval
in_practice.human_gate: Administrator approves each action and letter before it is sent or becomes effective.

evidence.claim: Agent acting on an expert-maintained rules base drafts contracts and sends them for signature

risks: Wrong contract chain count creates a permanent contract by accident
Templates out of date with a new CAO
Managers bypassing the form by mail
research_questions: How many days per action today, and where is the waiting?
Can AFAS workflows hold the contract chain rule for flex-to-employee conversions?
How often do templates change with CAO updates and who owns them?

tasks.short: Screen applications for eligibility: work permit, driving licence, code 95, VCA, availability for shifts.

today.trigger: A candidate applies in Recruitee or an agency proposes a worker.
steps: Open the application and CV in Recruitee
Check hard requirements: right to work, licence category, certificates, shift availability
Note gaps and ask the candidate for missing documents
Move the candidate to the next stage or flag to the recruiter
drudgery: Hunting for licence and certificate details in CVs
Asking for the same missing documents
today.time_sinks: Peaks in the season with many applications per day, and documents that arrive in pieces.

lenses.faster: A model lists which hard requirements each application shows and which are missing, with the source line; the administrator checks and decides, roughly halving reading time.
lenses.autonomous: An application starts the check; the summary and a request for missing documents are drafted, and the person decides the stage.
lenses.ambitious: Same-day eligibility checks for seasonal flex workers proposed by agencies, a group HR now barely checks itself; demand would grow in peak season.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses scanning CVs for a licence code; the administrator wants more time talking to candidates who are close.
lenses.options: Not for the decision; showing requirement gaps side by side helps but should not rank people.
lenses.altitude: The administrator owns the hard-requirement checklist per role with the recruiters; the selection decision stays human, job stays similar in expertise.
reach: Recruiter: first phone screen for warehouse roles (learn interview basics and how to probe availability)

tasks.human_edge: Judging unusual paths (foreign licences, equivalent certificates, gaps explained by care duties) and keeping the decision fair and explainable to the candidate.
tasks.pattern_why: Applicant evaluation is high-risk under the EU AI Act from December 2027 and GDPR Art. 22 bars a decision resting solely on automation; the person must lead.

in_practice.trigger: New application or agency proposal in Recruitee.
steps: Model extracts evidence for each hard requirement with the source text
Missing items shown and a document request drafted
Administrator reviews and sets the stage
Rejections use a template letter sent after the human decision
in_practice.human_gate: Every stage change and rejection is decided by the administrator or recruiter.

evidence.claim: Screening applicants is high-risk from 2 December 2027
The decision cannot rest solely on automated processing; letters can be automated

risks: Silent ranking creeping in through the summary
Bias against foreign certificates
Works council consent needed for tool processing applicant data
research_questions: Which hard requirements are truly binary for each warehouse and transport role?
Does Recruitee's own AI feature meet the EU AI Act high-risk duties by December 2027?
How many applications per week in peak season reach the administrator?

tasks.short: Answer staff questions on pay, leave, CAO rules, benefits, certificates and courses.

today.trigger: An employee or manager mails, calls, Teams-messages or walks in with a question.
steps: Work out who is asking and their contract and site
Look up the answer in the CAO, policy on SharePoint or the AFAS record
Reply by mail, Teams or phone
Pass harder questions to payroll or the HRBP
drudgery: The same questions on leave balance, payslip and holiday pay each week
today.time_sinks: Repeat questions and interruptions, peaking around payslip day and holiday allowance in May.

lenses.faster: Repeat policy questions are answered by a bot on owned content, balances come from a deterministic AFAS lookup; the administrator handles tickets and content, but the Danish data warns the gain is modest unless the workflow is redesigned.
lenses.autonomous: A question in Teams or WhatsApp starts it; the bot answers per CAO and site, says it is AI, and opens a ticket with the profile when it cannot answer.
lenses.ambitious: Answers for night-shift warehouse staff and flex workers who cannot reach HR during office hours, a group served for the first time; demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the tenth holiday-pay question; the administrator wants more time on the questions where someone is worried.
lenses.altitude: The administrator becomes owner of the HR knowledge base per CAO and site, deciding what the bot may answer; more expert.
reach: Payroll Specialist: first-line payslip explanation (learn payslip elements)
Learning and Development Specialist: answering course and certificate questions from Studytube

tasks.human_edge: Questions that hide sickness, debt, conflict or a resignation need a person who notices and responds with care.
tasks.pattern_why: A fixed flow: retrieve from owned content, one model call to answer, deterministic lookup for personal figures, ticket otherwise.

in_practice.trigger: Employee asks in Teams, the intranet or WhatsApp.
steps: Identify the employee and their CAO, site and contract
Retrieve from approved policy content and answer, citing the source
Quote personal balances from an AFAS lookup, never generated
Open a ticket with the profile when unsure or the topic is sensitive
in_practice.human_gate: Administrator handles tickets and signs off on content changes; sickness and health topics go straight to a person.
data_needed: Both CAOs and policies, structured per topic
in_practice.logs_to: Ticket queue and anonymised question log

evidence.claim: HR agent answers per region, contract and tenure with ticket escalation; 1,200 monthly users, CSAT 4.1
Chatbots alone saved about 3% of hours
Employee-facing bots must disclose they are AI
Works council consent needed when the bot uses personnel data

risks: Wrong answer on a CAO entitlement taken as a promise
Bot tone on sick leave
Question logs per employee seen as monitoring by the works council
research_questions: What share of last month's questions were repeat policy questions?
Can shop-floor staff sign in easily on their phones?
Will the OR consent under WOR art. 27(1)(k), and on what logging terms?

tasks.short: Process new hires: contract, AFAS record, payroll data, ID check, onboarding and course enrolments.

today.trigger: A candidate accepts an offer in Recruitee.
steps: Copy candidate data from Recruitee into AFAS
Draft the contract from the SharePoint template and send it for signature
Collect ID, bank details, tax form and certificates
Enrol in mandatory Studytube courses and inform site, IT and payroll
Check everything is ready before day one
drudgery: Chasing ID copies and signed contracts
today.time_sinks: Missing documents in the last days before the start date, especially in peak season.

lenses.faster: The Recruitee-to-AFAS handover, contract draft, Pocket app data request and course enrolments run automatically; the administrator checks the contract and the ID check, about 20 minutes per hire instead of one to two hours.
lenses.autonomous: Offer accepted starts it; data flows to AFAS, the contract is drafted, the new hire submits data in Pocket, and the administrator approves the contract and verifies identity.
lenses.ambitious: Every new starter, including seasonal hires, has a complete dossier and VCA and forklift training booked before day one, feeding 'onboarding completed in week one'; demand would grow in season.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses re-keying from Recruitee; the administrator wants more time making the first day go well.
lenses.options: Little; the contract follows the CAO.
lenses.altitude: The administrator owns the hire-to-day-one checklist and decides when a start can go ahead; more coordinating, similar expertise.
reach: Recruiter: offer letters and contract preparation (learn salary scale placement)
Learning and Development Specialist: booking mandatory onboarding training

tasks.human_edge: The ID and right-to-work check (Wet arbeid vreemdelingen) and spotting that a contract term or scale does not match what was promised.
tasks.pattern_why: The steps are the same for every hire and can be built as integrations and rules.

steps: Create the AFAS employee from Recruitee data
Generate the contract from the template and send for e-signature after approval
Send the Pocket app request for personal data and documents
Enrol mandatory Studytube courses by role and site
Show a readiness checklist with gaps three days before start
in_practice.human_gate: Administrator approves the contract and confirms the ID and right-to-work check.

evidence.claim: New hires submit data in the AFAS Pocket app before day one
Agent drafts contracts and sends them for signature on an expert rules base

risks: Integration breaks silently and a hire starts without a record
ID check reduced to a tick box
Wrong template for the transport versus warehouse CAO
research_questions: Is there a supported Recruitee to AFAS connector or must one be built?
What share of hires today start with an incomplete dossier?
How long does each step take per hire in peak season?

tasks.short: Look things up in employee files to answer managers and prepare personnel actions.

today.trigger: A manager, HRBP or payroll asks for facts from an employee's file.
steps: Find the employee in AFAS
Read through contracts, letters and notes in the dossier
Collect the facts: start date, contract history, warnings, certificates
Write them up and send to the requester
drudgery: Counting contract chain periods by hand
today.time_sinks: Long dossiers of employees with many contract extensions and transfers.

lenses.faster: A model builds a timeline from the dossier with links to each source document; the administrator checks the facts asked for, cutting search time by half or more.
lenses.autonomous: A request starts a draft fact sheet; the administrator checks access rights and content before anything leaves HR.
lenses.ambitious: A monthly contract-chain and expiry check across all fixed-term and flex workers, so HRBPs decide on extensions in time instead of by surprise; demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses scrolling dossiers; the administrator wants more time answering the real question behind the request.
lenses.altitude: The administrator decides what a requester may see from a file and owns the fact-sheet format; more expert in privacy.
reach: HR Business Partner: preparing case files for dismissal or performance talks (learn what a sound dossier needs)
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: contract expiry reports

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what a manager is entitled to see (need to know under AVG) and noticing what is missing from a file.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call turns a dossier into a cited timeline inside a fixed request flow.

in_practice.trigger: Request logged by a manager, HRBP or payroll.
steps: Check the requester's role and access rights
Model drafts a timeline and answer with links to source documents
Administrator verifies against the sources and removes what is not needed
Send and log the disclosure
in_practice.human_gate: Administrator approves every answer before it is sent.

evidence.claim: Models summarise documents into cited timelines
Health data is special-category and should stay out of prompts

risks: Over-disclosure to managers
Hallucinated facts in a dismissal case
Health notes in the dossier sent to a model
research_questions: How many such requests per week and how long each takes?
Can AFAS export dossiers to a model without the health categories?
Which request types are most frequent?

tasks.short: Chase managers, employees and agencies for missing documents, signatures, certificates and hours.

today.trigger: A dossier, payroll close or audit shows something missing.
steps: Make a list of what is missing and from whom
Mail or call each person or agency
Track replies in Excel
Remind again and escalate to the manager
File what comes in
drudgery: Keeping the tracking spreadsheet up to date
today.time_sinks: Repeated reminders to shift staff and busy managers, and agencies that send documents late.

lenses.faster: Gaps are found automatically and reminders go out on a schedule in the right language; the administrator only deals with people who do not respond, about half the effort.
lenses.autonomous: A nightly completeness check starts it; personalised requests and reminders go out by mail, Teams or the Pocket app, and escalation to the manager waits for the administrator's approval.
lenses.ambitious: A weekly completeness report per site for site managers and the three agencies, a service they do not have now; demand would grow before audits.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the tracking spreadsheet; the administrator wants more time solving why the same site is always late.
lenses.altitude: The administrator sets the rules for what must be in each file and when to escalate, and owns the agency document agreement; more coordinating.
reach: Bookkeeper: chasing agencies for corrected invoices and hours (learn the agency contracts)
Learning and Development Specialist: chasing expired certificates

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which manager or agency contact responds to what, and when a missing document signals a bigger problem.
tasks.pattern_why: Who to ask, through which channel and when to escalate varies per case; a person approves escalations.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly completeness check against the required-document list.
steps: List gaps per employee, manager and agency
Send a personalised request through the best channel
Remind on a schedule and file documents that arrive
Propose escalation after the deadline
in_practice.human_gate: Administrator approves escalations to managers and agencies and reviews documents that fail validation.
data_needed: Required-document list per role and contract type
in_practice.logs_to: Request and reminder log per employee in AFAS

risks: Reminder spam annoying managers
Agencies ignoring automated mails
Messages to wrong person disclosing data
research_questions: How many open document requests are tracked at a time and how long they stay open?
Will agencies accept a portal or mail flow for documents?
Which channel do warehouse staff actually respond to?

role.altitude: The HR Administrator moves from typing and filing to running exception queues, owning the HR knowledge base per CAO and site, and keeping dossier and document rules. They gain the right to reject incomplete requests and to decide what the employee bot may answer, so the job becomes more expert in data quality, AVG and CAO rules.
reach: Payroll Specialist: pre-close checks of personnel changes and first-line payslip questions
Learning and Development Specialist: certificate expiry and mandatory course enrolment
Recruiter: offer and contract preparation for warehouse roles
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: AFAS data-quality rules and contract expiry reports
Bookkeeper: matching agency hours and invoices
role.ceiling_note: Roughly 40 to 50 percent of the hours on these tasks can return, but only if workflows are redesigned (self-service, integrations) rather than a bot added beside the old process. Limits are works council consent, AVG on health data, the human ID and selection decisions, and how well the policy content is owned.
skills_to_grow: Writing and structuring knowledge-base content per CAO
AVG and works council rules for HR data and AI
Basic process measurement (days per action, first-time-right)
role.ambitious_version: The two administrators run an HR service desk that serves all 1,200 staff plus flex workers around the clock: a disclosed AI front door on owned content, dossiers complete before day one, nightly certificate and contract-chain checks per site, and a weekly completeness report to site managers and agencies, with the administrators handling the cases that need a person.
